narrative.overview:
A dark, precise working surface where the shipped work is the hero. The world is committed dark (`color-scheme: dark`): a graphite ground, warm off-white ink, gilt for labels and the one primary action, and a single ruby mark as the only bold colour. The interface steps back so real screenshots of live client sites carry the page: they are dealt as a 3D deck in the hero, and they sit in hairline frames on every project card. Nothing on the surface is illustration; the imagery is the evidence.

The register is calm, exact, and workmanlike. Headings are Schibsted Grotesk, tight and confident at 600–700; every piece of data (stacks, context tags, hostnames, form labels, button labels) speaks in uppercase DM Mono. Depth is tonal: one step from ground to surface, drawn with 1px hairlines. The exception is physical layering: a phone capture laid over a desktop screenshot, screenshots stacked in the hero deck, and the portrait badge hanging on its strap each cast a soft shadow, because they really sit on top of something.

Density is generous and editorial: a centered 72rem column, wide vertical rhythm, sections divided by full-width hairlines, lists divided by hairlines instead of boxed into cards. The surface is alive with light and motion: a field of gilt mono glyphs flowing behind the hero, a name that decodes itself under a ruby caret, screenshots dealt and re-shuffled as a deck, a crosshair that measures the contact page. Each page gets its own effects rather than one global trick. Effects are welcome and meant to show craft, but they are always drawn from the palette (gilt light, ruby as a trace, ink on graphite). The world still refuses rainbow neon, candy accents, and the generic Swiss-Helvetica grid it replaced.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite dark world, committed (`color-scheme: dark`), warm off-white ink.
Real screenshots of shipped sites are the imagery; no placeholders, no illustration.
One ruby accent, used as a single mark: never a fill, never a wall.
Gilt for mono labels, the one primary action, and the selected/hover state.
Two voices: Schibsted Grotesk (display/body) + DM Mono (all data/labels).
Depth by tonal step + hairlines; soft shadows only where something physically sits on something else.
Expressive light and motion (shaders, glyph fields, type reveals, 3D decks), tinted from the palette, chosen per page, fully opt-out.

rules.name: The Single Mark Rule
rules.body: Ruby appears only as a mark: a dot, a short rule, a link, a focus ring. It never fills a surface. The closing CTA is a graphite panel with a gilt button, not a ruby band; if ruby covers an area larger than a dot or a line, the rule is broken.

rules.name: The Gilt Job Rule
rules.body: Gilt has three jobs: mono labels, the single primary action, and interactive state (hover/selected borders, hostname links). It is never body text, never a heading, never a large fill.

rules.name: The Context Mark Rule
rules.body: How a project came about is shown by who it was with, never a colour wash: Freelance is a 0.4rem ruby dot plus the word; macmac and Marvelous Digital appear as their own wordmarks, monochrome in `currentColor` (`ContextBadge.astro`, SVGs in `src/components/icons/`), with the name as screen-reader text. Sizes: 0.62rem (macmac) / 0.92rem (Marvelous) in caption lines and chips, ~1.4/1.9rem on the About page. Never recolour or restyle the partner wordmarks.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Prose and headings are Schibsted Grotesk; anything that reads as data (labels, stacks, tags, hostnames, buttons) is DM Mono, uppercase, tracked. A voice never crosses into the other's job.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone. No mono kicker or label sits above a section heading; mono labels only name data next to it (a `dt` beside its `dd`, a context tag above a card title that it describes).

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by a 1px `line` border and one tonal step, never by a shadow. A shadow only ever marks a literal physical overlap: something resting on, or hanging in front of, something else.

dos: Do let real screenshots of shipped sites be the imagery; crop them to 16:10 (desktop) or 390:844 (phone), top-anchored, inside a hairline frame.
Do keep ruby as a single mark: dots, a short rule, links, focus rings.
Do use gilt for mono labels, the one primary action, and hover/selected state.
Do show project context with the ContextBadge (freelance dot or partner wordmark) wherever context appears.
Do separate surfaces with the `line` hairline and one tonal step; divide lists with hairlines instead of boxing them into cards.
Do put all data (stacks, tags, hostnames, labels, buttons) in DM Mono, uppercase, tracked.
Do draw icons as inline SVG strokes (1.5px, square caps) sized in `em`.

Do gate every animation behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` with an intentional still alternative, give long-running content motion a pause control, and stop loops and shaders when off-screen or the tab is hidden.
Do tint every glow, shader, and light effect from the palette: gilt as the light, ruby only as a trace, screen/additive blending over graphite.
Do keep content in the HTML and visible without JS; effects decorate it (`aria-hidden` layers, a CSS failsafe for anything hidden before it animates).
Do ship every visitor-facing string in both EN and FR (binding product constraint).
donts: Don't fill a surface with ruby or build a ruby band; the closing CTA is a graphite panel with a gilt button.
Don't add drop shadows for elevation; shadows only mark physical layering (the phone capture, the hero deck, the hanging badge).
Don't use placeholder imagery or stock illustration in place of real work. The only portrait is Thomas's real photo (`src/assets/portrait.jpg`, About page).
Don't put a mono eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't use unicode glyph arrows (→ ↗) or emoji as icons.
Don't use off-palette glows, rainbow or saturated neon gradients, or a second bold accent.
Don't set body or heading text in gilt, or run prose in the mono voice.
Don't let an effect cut text contrast below AA, tint the screenshots themselves, or add heavy runtime dependencies when a small hand-written island does the job.
Don't add a second display typeface or a system font; the pairing is fixed.
